lines.trans: Hello, tell me, did a tall man stop by your shop this morning?
In a black coat and with a moustache?
Yes, it seems there was someone like that.
And what did he buy?
An engagement ring.
Do you have the exact same one?
Who is that guy with Vika?
Probably a masseur. Vika forgot the business card on the table.
He does not look like a masseur! You said yourself that Vika wants sex.
Max, are you a fool? It says: massage!
Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Говорят, что мысли материальны.
examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Таня, мне вечером хватает сил только поесть и помыться.
examples.trans: Tanya, in the evening I only have enough strength to eat and wash up.

examples.text: Шеф, мы вас ждём. Мы просто хотели, чтобы вы нам помогли.
examples.trans: Chef, we are waiting for you. We just wanted you to help us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'против').

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно напротив и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite across from and calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну, погоди. Домой доедешь?
examples.trans: Well, wait. Will you make it home?

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.
examples.trans: You know what, you had better spend the night at home.

examples.text: Рядом с цветочным, через дорогу.
examples.trans: Next to the flower shop, across the street.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне тоже больно, я вас не заметила.
examples.trans: It hurts me too, I did not notice you.

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

examples.text: Похоже, что можно! Тогда я тоже поздравляю.
examples.trans: It looks like we can! Then I congratulate you too.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('massage').

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень массажный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very massage choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алон'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salon, parlor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

examples.text: Можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon.

examples.text: Салон машины белый.
examples.trans: The car's interior is white.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.

examples.text: Слушай, ты можешь отключить этот противный звук?
examples.trans: Listen, can you turn off that annoying sound?

examples.text: Витя, это фиаско!
examples.trans: Vitya, this is a fiasco!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Походу, шеф собирается Елене сделать предложение!
examples.trans: It looks like the chef is going to propose to Elena!

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Шеф сделает предложение!
examples.trans: The chef will make a proposal!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё хорошо, девочки.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, girls.

examples.text: Вечно вы всё портите!
examples.trans: You always ruin everything!

examples.text: Да нет, ребят, тут всё понятно.
examples.trans: No, guys, everything is clear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, очень приятно.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, that is very nice.

examples.text: Костян, скажи, а правда, что беременным секса больше хочется?
examples.trans: Kostyan, tell me, is it true that pregnant women want sex more?

examples.text: Сестра Вики сказала, что Вика хочет.
examples.trans: Vika's sister said that Vika wants it.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Нет, я всё сделаю очень аккуратно.
examples.trans: No, I will do everything very carefully.

examples.text: Сделаю всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: I will do everything very carefully!

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Говорят, что мысли материальны.
examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.

examples.text: Звони в любое время! Ладно, я пойду.
examples.trans: Call at any time! Alright, I will go.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'heard', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Я сам слышал! Так, Настя, набери-ка его!
examples.trans: I heard it myself! Right, Nastya, dial his number!

examples.text: Я ничего не слышал.
examples.trans: I didn't hear anything.

examples.text: Ты меня слышишь?
examples.trans: Can you hear me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Так я тушёнку привёз.
examples.trans: Well I brought canned stewed meat.

examples.text: Никаких. Спартак сегодня не играет.
examples.trans: None at all. Spartak is not playing today.

examples.text: Будущую? Я ещё не в таком статусе.
examples.trans: Future? I am not in that status yet.

meanings.en: to gather, collect, rack up (views, points)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'dial, call', paired with 'набирать'.

examples.text: Ролик уже набрал четыре миллиона просмотров!
examples.trans: The clip has already got four million views!

examples.text: Я наберу твой номер.
examples.trans: I'll dial your number.

examples.text: Мы наберём много лайков в интернете.
examples.trans: We will gather many likes on the internet.
